note: Dated events for the public-record timeline. Only facts already checked against the cited source.

events.title: Largest-installer wind-down
events.detail: Sunlight said one of its largest installers was winding down its operations and expected to impair $30–33 million of advances to that installer.

events.title: State attorneys general letter
events.detail: Nine state attorneys general wrote to five solar lenders, including Sunlight Financial and Cross River Bank, about Pink Energy customers whose systems were never installed or do not work properly.

source.label: State attorneys general letter to solar lenders, November 22, 2022

events.title: Negative platform fees
events.detail: Sunlight recognized $22.7 million in negative platform fees in the three months ended December 31, 2022.

events.title: EBITDA requirement missed; loan cap exceeded
events.detail: Sunlight did not meet the EBITDA requirement of its SVB revolving facility, and the Bank Partner's funded but unsold loans exceeded the loan cap in the Bank Partner agreements.

events.title: Facilities restructured
events.detail: Sunlight entered amended Bank Partner agreements and a new secured term loan, and the SVB facility was repaid and terminated.

events.title: Chapter 11 filed
events.detail: Sunlight filed Chapter 11 petitions in the United States Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware.

events.title: Emergence from Chapter 11
events.detail: Sunlight completed its Chapter 11 restructuring; a consortium including affiliates of Greenbacker Capital Management, Sunstone Credit and IGS Ventures, together with Cross River Bank, owns 100% of the company.

source.label: Sunlight Financial emergence press release, December 7, 2023
